subject: Post-demo recap: model recommendations + streaming behavior notes
snippet: Recap of model suggestions, attached prompt sets + benchmarks, and next steps to triage streaming partial-output issues.
messages:
From: Elena Kovacs <elena.kovacs@mediarise.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 23:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up & test artifacts from today's demo

Hi Connor (and Alex),

Thanks for the demo earlier — great walkthrough. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we start scoping the PoC: 

- We care mostly about customer-facing summarization and an interactive assistant embedded in our product. Primary concerns: hallucination on long contexts, partial-sentence outputs when streaming, and occasional latency burps.
- I attached a small prompt set (mediarise_prompt_set_v1.csv) that shows typical product descriptions + user queries.
- Can you recommend 2–3 model candidates for our initial eval (balance of cost vs. quality)? Also, if you have any bench numbers (latency @ 1/5/20 tokens, token cost estimates) that would be helpful.

We have a security review next week so please flag anything that would affect SSO/KMS/retention.

Thanks — happy to hop on another 30-min call if needed.

Best,
Elena
Product Ops | Mediarise

Attachment: mediarise_prompt_set_v1.csv (text/csv, 28KB)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elena Kovacs <elena.kovacs@mediarise.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & test artifacts from today's demo

Hi Elena — really appreciate you sending the prompt set. Short recap + concrete next steps so we can move toward a focused eval: 

Recap of suggested model candidates (tradeoffs):
- redwood-instruct-13b-v2 (recommended starter): strong summarization, good latency on 80–128 token responses, robust against mild prompt perturbations. Cost: mid-tier.
- mistral-instruct-7b (cost-efficient): lower token cost, slightly weaker on long-context coherence but good for interactive assist flows.
- llama-3-13b-8k (quality-first): best coherence on long contexts in our internal benchmarks, higher cost and memory.

Benchmarks & artifacts: I uploaded a short benchmark PDF with rough latency and token-cost estimates for each model on our hosted offering (benchmark-overview-20270414.pdf). These are conservative numbers (p95) for the model + streaming path. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/mediarise-evals-2027-04

Streaming UX notes (seen during today's demo):
- Partial/sliced outputs: we observed the client receiving truncated fragments mid-sentence when stop sequences were triggered or when a streaming chunk boundary coincided with the model sampling step.
- Stop sequences: default client-side stop handling sometimes closes the stream early if punctuation tokens align with stop tokens.
- Latency spikes: occasional 200–400ms spikes on first token when batching and cache warmup coincide.

Immediate mitigation plan (for PoC):
1) Recommended model for PoC: redwood-instruct-13b-v2 (pick this unless you want to prioritize cost).
2) Suggest we run a 3-model A/B eval: redwood-instruct-13b-v2 vs mistral-instruct-7b vs llama-3-13b-8k across your prompt set. We can provide pre-filled eval harness + scripts.
3) Streaming UX fixes (quick): server-side enforcement of stop tokens (avoid client-only), increase stream_chunk_size to prefer fewer, larger chunks, and set a 50ms minimum emission delay to avoid mid-word breaks.

Next steps / asks from you:
- Confirm which models you want in the 3-model run.
- Tell us the target SLA for p95 latency and cost constraints per 1k tokens (helps us narrow config).
- Security checklist items: confirm if you need us to provide KMS integration docs and SOC2 artifacts (we can attach immediately).

I'll loop Grace (infra/solutions) who'll help with streaming tuning and the eval harness. Available for a 30-min call tomorrow if that helps.

Thanks,
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: benchmark-overview-20270414.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Kovacs <elena.kovacs@mediarise.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & test artifacts from today's demo

Hi Elena — quick technical note from the infra side on the streaming quirks you saw and a proposed configuration we can push for the PoC: 

Observed behavior summary (from demo logs / replay):
- Fragmentation: when stream_chunk_size = 64 tokens and emission is immediate, we saw mid-word halting on ~2% of sample requests where the sampling step returned a control token.
- Stop token misfires: client-side stop filtering combined with punctuation-based stops caused early termination for ~0.7% of cases in the prompt set where product descriptions end in ellipses or bullet fragments.
- Latency spike root cause: concurrent batch assembly + KV cache miss for cold keys — first token pays a setup penalty for a small subset of requests.

Recommended PoC streaming config (we can deploy these on your dedicated test namespace):
- Server-side stop enforcement: enforce stop sequences at the model host and emit an explicit <STOP> event. This prevents client libraries from prematurely closing streams.
- stream_chunk_size: set to 128 tokens for product summary workloads (reduces chunk boundary frequency).
- emission_throttle_ms: set soft throttle of 40–60ms to avoid splitting in-word outputs; empirically reduces mid-word breaks without detectable UX regressions.
- Warmup policy: enable per-user KV-cache pinning (5 warmup requests) to reduce cold first-token spikes.
- Monitoring hooks: we will add a streaming-specific metric (stream_fragment_rate) to the eval dashboard and add alerting for fragment_rate > 0.5% (per 10k requests).

Action items we can take immediately (48–72 hours):
1) Provision a scoped test namespace with the three models and the streaming config above.
2) Run the prompt set across the models and produce: token-level latency histogram, fragment incidence table, and example transcripts where stop tokens triggered unexpectedly.
3) Produce a small recommended prompt rewrite doc (2–3 patterns) that reduces stop-token collisions for your copy style.

If you confirm the PoC window (two weeks preferred) we will schedule the runs and deliver the results + suggested rollout configuration.

Cheers,
Grace
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Target constraints: p95 latency <= 450ms for 64-token responses, cost goal <= $12 per 1k tokens (for initial evaluation). Two-week PoC window works. Please attach the SOC2/KMS docs and the prompt-rewrite doc when available.

We'll sign the PoC intake form and booking request by end of day — happy for a kickoff call tomorrow at 10am PT.
